items.title: 18.10.1 Reaction of Acidified Manganate(VII) Ions with Ethanedioate Ions

source_refs.note: Topic 18.10.1 (PDF 33). The printed overall equation (8H+, 5Mn2+, 2CO2) and multipliers are corrected; the printed E of +0.49 V for CO2/C2O4 2- is kept and the usual -0.49 V noted. Flagged for review.

blocks.text: For the reaction between acidified manganate(VII) (permanganate) ions and ethanedioate (oxalate) ions, compare the two reduction half-reactions as given in the book:

The half-reaction with the more positive E proceeds as a reduction, so MnO4- is reduced to Mn2+ (the oxidising agent) and C2O4 2- is oxidised to CO2 (the reducing agent). The electrons lost must equal the electrons gained, so the reduction half-equation is multiplied by 2 and the oxidation half-equation by 5:

items: With the book's values, E cell = 1.52 - 0.49 = +1.03 V, so the reaction is feasible.

blocks.title: Check the printed values
blocks.text: The book prints the overall equation as 2MnO4- + 5C2O4 2- + 8H+ -> 5Mn2+ + 2CO2 + 8H2O and says the oxidation half is multiplied by 2; both are slips, and the balanced equation above has 16H+, 2Mn2+ and 10CO2. Data tables usually give about -0.49 V (not +0.49 V) for the CO2/ethanedioate couple, which would make E cell about 1.52 - (-0.49) = +2.01 V. Either way E cell is positive and the reaction is feasible.

blocks.prompt: In the reaction of MnO4- with C2O4 2-, which species is the reducing agent and what is it oxidised to?
blocks.explanation: The ethanedioate ion, C2O4 2-; it is oxidised to carbon dioxide.

items: MnO4- (+1.52 V) is reduced to Mn2+; C2O4 2- is oxidised to CO2.
